Cancel anytime. “Margo!” From hearing the name inside the store to being called out while on errands and in grocery stores, Jill Furman, owner and operator of Margo Metaphysical, is commonly and incorrectly referred to as “Margo.” But she doesn’t mind, it just means they met her on a whim while she was working. After sleeping in, at 10:30 a.m., Furman arrives at her storefront on Clayton Street with her 2-year-old golden retriever, Luna. Paperwork, bills, emails and around 11 a.m., helping customers whether they’re looking for something in particular or just wanting to chat. Since 2002, Margo Metaphysical has served the community in downtown Athens, Georgia, and beyond. From the 305 to the 706 Furman hasn’t always lived in Athens; in fact, it wasn’t until after having her children and wanting to raise them in “a calmer, less materialistic, less cutthroat environment” that she considered moving away from Miami, Florida. So, she made a list of college towns, visiting each one and settling on Athens. After moving to the Classic City, she also pivoted in her career, going from a teacher to all-in on a wholesale amber business she previously started with her husband called Amber Dreams. Part of the job involved attending gem and mineral shows and meeting dealers. From Africans selling Congolese statues and malachite to Pakistanis selling onyx, Furman was impassioned by the interactions. “I was like, wait a minute, this is what I want to be doing,” Furman recalled. With a storefront for Amber Dreams across from Mellow Mushroom, everything was set in motion and only picked up speed when the Clayton Street spot went up for lease. “I can’t let this spot go,” Furman thought. A manager in each spot, Furman ran between each store, Amber Dreams and Margo Metaphysical, named after a combination of her daughters’ names, Maya and Arielle. A few years later, as a result of a divorce from her husband, he kept Amber Dreams and Furman put all of her focus into Margo Metaphysical. “[I thought,] if I can have it in my control, it can be great,’ so the store has prospered. We don’t make a lot of money, but we serve a lot of people in the community, and we’re slow and steady,” Furman said. As a result of this prosperity, she was able to buy the building in 2023, “and the store is paying for itself.” More than just crystals “Crystals, books, journals. I mean, this is just me with or without owning the store. I’m an old hippie.” Since she was a little girl, going gemstone mining and picking up rocks and crystals and filling her pockets with them when she went on hikes, Furman remembers having an interest in the metaphysical, also referred to as “woo woo stuff.” An array of crystals and gemstones inside Margo Metaphysical located on Clayton Street, in Athens, Georgia, on April 7, 2026. (Photo/Caroline Newbern) Caroline Newbern “I was always like the one who, “Oh, I don’t need a pillow and a blanket to go hiking. I need room in my backpack for whatever we find along the way,” Furman said. This love for traveling carries over into the careful curation of Margo Metaphysical. There are hand-picked lamps from Istanbul, moldavite from Czechoslovakia and papyrus from Egypt. “I have to see it. I have to feel the energy,” Furman said. She plans for six trips a year, three trips and three gem and mineral shows, like the anticipated May show in Franklin, North Carolina. After “filling the car,” she drives back. Despite the consideration of “woo woo energy” or other conservatism toward the metaphysical, Furman treats the stones, crystals, journals, sound and energy healing sessions as tools. “You know, if somebody is going to be more confident by having Tiger’s Eye, which says it makes you more confident, why would we not accept that confidence?” “We do not replace doctors, we do not replace therapists, but we’re here to give an ear for whatever is ailing people…but the stones, the journals, the tools, they’re all self help tools, give love to thyself,” Furman said. A stone from outer space “The most conservative people that aren't into crystals at all will come in here and buy a beautiful bracelet or a beautiful ring. But a lot of times I get people to feel this,” Furman said. On the counter, Furman placed a stand of three small pieces of moldavite, a green formed from melted rock ejected into the atmosphere an estimated 15 million years ago by a meteorite. “It’s a very energetic stone from Czechoslovakia. A lot of people who’ve never felt energy and stones will feel something,” Furman said. Moldavite, considered to be an “extremely transformational stone,” can cause a sensation of heat, tingling or pulsing. And while not everyone feels it, others may feel too much and experience a sense of anxiety. Most feel calm and peaceful, in addition to productive energy that goes into their day. She recalled touching it when she was younger; beforehand, she aligned with the conservatism, anti-”woo woo,” thought that people were making things up. “Until I felt that stone. And then I'm like, ‘Wait, there's something to this.’ And then I started opening my mind to it,” Furman said. “And if it’s 10% true and 90% what we do with thinking it’s true? I’ll take that.” Community care In addition to its metaphysical offerings, Furman is focused on giving back to the community. “The art we go by [is] a Buddhist philosophy of doing at least three kind things a day…the more you give, the more you get back, spiritually, emotionally and financially,” she said. Whether that be lending an ear or donating to various causes, Furman, straying from materialism and preferring company over presents, exemplifies this principle; while the store runs itself, Furman has refused a salary for about three years. Jill Furman and her dog Luna pose for a portrait inside Margo Metaphysical located on Clayton Street, in Athens, Georgia, on April 7, 2026. (Photo/Caroline Newbern) Caroline Newbern “I’d rather give away everything I can,” she said. Luna also helps out where she can as an “emotional support shop dog.” “People come in here with angst and anxiety and difficulties and just fears or whatever is going on with them, they'll end up on the floor in an embrace with her,” Furman said. Photograph: Yves Herman/Reuters Europe Europeans want a united Europe but question whether it can get there, study finds A continent-wide crisis of confidence is creating fertile ground for far-right narratives of decline, report suggests Jon Henley Europe correspondent Wed 9 Sep 2026 01.00 EDT Last modified on Wed 9 Sep 2026 03.46 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Europeans overwhelmingly want a strong, united and independent Europe but question whether it can get there, according to a study that suggests a continent-wide crisis of confidence is creating fertile ground for far-right narratives of decline. The report , based on 5,800 interviews in France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland and the UK and analysis of the way Europe is discussed in the politics and media of 15 countries, paints a picture of an ambitious but disillusioned public. It found that 68% of respondents spoke about Europe in terms of a “general deterioration or loss of normality”, compared with just 12% who said they viewed the present moment as a time of “European awakening and renewal”. Many recognised the major challenges facing Europe, including war (43%), economic pressures (33%) and the need for greater international autonomy (29%). But 74% said Europe was not dealing well with them, and 56% believed its future was “in danger”. The problem is not lack of ambition: an overwhelming 73% of respondents harbour a strong European vision of unity and political integration (35%), peace and security (28%) or prosperity (19%), while only 13% hope for “less Europe” or EU dissolution. For many, said the study’s author, Paweł Zerka, a senior fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR) thinktank, the problem was “not that they’ve stopped wanting a stronger Europe, but that they no longer believe it’s achievable”. The result, Zerka added, was an “imagination gap. People can picture the kind of Europe they want, but struggle to imagine a credible path from where it is today to where they want it to be. These are matters of policy, not just communication.” View image in fullscreen Ursula von der Leyen, the president of the European Commission. Photograph: Mads Claus Rasmussen/Reuters A week before the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, is due to deliver her annual “state of the union” address in Brussels, Zerka said the evidence suggested the bloc needed “fewer grand promises” and more “proof of trajectory” . The study cites dozens of conversations with Europeans. “I’m regularly relieved I live in Europe. It’s not perfect and some things are going in the wrong direction, but no region in the world is safer, freer and more democratic,” one German said. However, while he identified the climate crisis and far-right parties as the continent’s greatest challenges, he said they were not being tackled effectively. “Elections focus too much on the here and now, and not enough on the future,” he said. The respondent said he would like Europe in 20 years’ time to be “free, democratic, sustainable, less indebted, politically further to the left [and] peaceful”. Asked whether he thought that was likely to happen, he said: “No.” The study classed Europe’s voters in four categories. The Positives (19%) are staunch pro-Europeans who view current crises as a catalyst for a stronger, more integrated union. The Negatives (39%) believe Europe’s best days are behind it. Almost half of people in France, Germany and Italy – and almost all who voted for radical-right parties such as Germany’s AfD, France’s RN, the Dutch PVV and Reform UK – were Negatives, with 83% speaking of Europe in terms of loss and decline. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to This is Europe The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment after newsletter promotion The Disconnected (12%) are generally apathetic voters for whom EU integration is distant background noise, and the Uncertain (31%) share pro-European values but doubt the continent’s ability to act decisively, keep citizens safe or uphold its values. Almost a third (32%) of respondents across all countries surveyed mentioned “Europe’s slowness” in their responses. As one young Polish citizen, born in the 2000s, put it bluntly: “The EU fundamentally discusses a lot, but does nothing.” The bloc’s failure to stand its ground when confronted by powerful actors was also a recurring theme, mentioned by almost a third (30%) of all respondents, with the EU’s recent tariff concessions to Donald Trump a particularly humiliating symbol. Zerka said the Uncertain group was key to the future trajectory of Europe. “Leaders tend to preach to the Positives or bow down to the Negatives,” he said, but it “is among the ‘uncertain’ where belief in Europe’s future remains up for grabs.” Unlike hardened Eurosceptics, Uncertain voters retain a strong emotional attachment to the European project, the report argues, but are alienated by institutional inertia, bureaucratic slowness and perceived geopolitical weakness. Winning back those doubters would require politicians to demonstrate that collective European action can solve tangible domestic crises, from energy security and defence to climate change and the cost of living crisis, Zerka said. https://stuyspec.com/article/art-beyond-.text: News Subsections Arts and Entertainment Art Beyond Representation A look into notable works at the Art Institute of Chicago’s Beyond Form: Abstraction at Midcentury and the shift away from realism in response to global political change. Reading Time: 4 minute s By Sasha Silakov Issue 1 , Volume 117 || 2026 - 2027 As the world moved from the 19th century into the tumultuous 20th, artists increasingly abandoned the conventions of representation, seeking new forms of expression capable of capturing a world defined by political upheaval and unprecedented violence that literal representation appeared insufficient to capture. Rather than relying on recognizable subjects to convey meaning, abstract artists foregrounded formal elements such as color, line, shape, texture, and composition, challenging the assumption that art must reproduce or directly reference the visible world. The unprecedented scale of wartime destruction and human suffering created a time in which literal representation appeared insufficient. This shift became particularly significant in the United States following World War II, when American Abstract Expressionism emerged as a dominant force in the international art world. New York replaced Paris as a major art hub, elevating artists such as Jackson Pollock, Mark Rothko, and Willem de Kooning to international prominence. Yet this narrative often positions American abstraction as the culmination of modernist experimentation. It is not. The Art Institute of Chicago’s Beyond Form: Abstraction at Midcentury is a direct challenge to this Western narrative, placing artists from historically underrepresented regions and backgrounds alongside the figures who have traditionally dominated the canon of midcentury abstraction. Abstract Expressionism, as popularized in postwar society, is certainly not devoid of a diverse set of nationalities. Mark Rothko, known for his color field paintings, was born to a Jewish family in Latvia. Willem de Kooning, who headed an abstract style known as action painting, moved from Rotterdam to the United States at age 24. Despite their disparate backgrounds, both artists became part of the New York School, a group of abstract expressionists. Although a number of the American abstract expressionists were, in fact, immigrants and war veterans, their proximity to each other for exchange of ideas, as well as their location in one of the most culturally prominent cities, certainly augmented their fame as abstract expressionists. As both of these aforementioned artists are displayed in Beyond Form: Abstraction at Midcentury , a plethora of lesser-known artists are placed alongside them. A prime example is Hélio Oiticica, a Brazilian painter and sculptor, often attributed to the beginning of the Neo-Concrete movement in Brazil. Metaesquema, No. 244 (1957), Oiticica’s gouache-on-cardboard painting, exemplifies the exhibition's goal to complicate the conventional narrative of midcentury abstraction. Metaesquema, No. 244 , showing red and blue semicircles on cardboard, is part of Oiticica’s broader Metaesquema series, with over 350 geometric works created between 1957 and 1958. He worked with the Grupo Frente in Rio de Janeiro, a group of Brazilian artists in the 1950s. The Metaesquema series sought to completely rid the cardboard medium of “representation.” He eliminated surface texture and color modulation, an art technique that artificially creates light and shadow to purposefully flatten the painting. Oiticica treated art not as a medium for representation, but instead as an autonomous “concrete” object. The devastation of World War II fundamentally altered artists’ understanding of representation, as the Holocaust and the rise of the atomic age challenged the ability of traditional artistic forms to communicate the realities of modern life. Artists began to experience deep senses of absurdity and existentialism, leading them to focus on internal emotional truths. Pollock and Rothko, for example, focused on the action of painting itself as a subject. Literal recreations of the external world became inadequate to convey the atrocities of the time. For artists such as Otto Piene, this crisis of representation necessitated not merely a new style, but a new conception of what art could become in the postwar world. Born in Weimar Germany in 1928, Piene was only a teenager when he was drafted into World War II as an anti-aircraft gunner. His time on the front lines shaped his later artistic works, as after the war he created a series of so-called fire paintings, burning liquid solvent over a red-pigmented canvas. The scorched surface of Fire Painting (1967) evokes the same feelings of devastation that Piene saw in artillery fire and explosions of bombs during wartime. The choice that Beyond Form: Abstraction at Midcentury makes to display Fire Painting is certainly a strong one; black burn marks and the solid red eye-catching against the light walls of the gallery, as if one can feel the heat emanating from dropped explosives with every closer step. But while Piene was forced to fight for Germany, other artists featured in Beyond Form: Abstraction at Midcentury instead based their art on their forced migrations away from war-torn Europe. Romanian-born Jewish artist Hedda Sterne left Bucharest for New York in 1941 after bearing witness to the Bucharest Pogrom and the rise of Nazism in Europe. In her new home, Sterne was featured in exhibitions of the New York School and worked closely with many abstract expressionists, even being featured as the only woman in an image of a group of abstract artists called the Irascible 18. Although Sterne did not identify as an abstract expressionist, she was influential at the New York School for her use of spray paint as a medium. Beyond Form: Abstraction at Midcentury , however, moves away from some of her more popular works and features Untitled (1950), watercolor on paper. The watercolor application creates bursts of color that somewhat resemble a figure in motion as she explored art in her new urban environment. If you’re ever in the area, make sure to visit the Art Institute of Chicago. Right next to the Michigan Avenue entrance, Beyond Form: Abstraction at Midcentury , on view until October 19, reminds us that Abstract Expressionism emerged as a truly global movement in response to a world rebuilding itself after near destruction, becoming the gateway for future artistic movements to center not just the external world, but our interiority as well.

https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachric.text: SANTHERA PHARMACEUTICALS HOLDING AG Nachrichten Analysen Kurse Chart Santhera Pharmaceuticals Holding AG: Santhera Pharmaceuticals Half Year Results for the six months ending 30 June 2026 Ad hoc announcement pursuant to Art. 53 LR. A conference call will be held on September 30, 2026, at 14:00 CEST / 13:00 BST / 08:00 EDT. Details are at the end of this news release Strong momentum and expanding global access position AGAMREE for continued growth Pratteln, Switzerland, September 30, 2026 - Santhera Pharmaceuticals (SIX: SANN) announces the Company's financial results for the six months ended June 30, 2026. Orlando Oliveira, CEO of Santhera said : "We made strong progress in the first half of 2026, with growing commercial momentum for AGAMREE and significant advances in patient access globally. In Europe, pricing and reimbursement agreements in Spain and Italy mean that AGAMREE is now commercially available in four of the five major EU markets, while our agreement with Nxera significantly expands our reach across key APAC territories. Importantly, the long-term data presented in March further reinforced AGAMREE 's differentiated profile in DMD and has supported increased physician adoption. With our partners also continuing to rapidly expand access across their territories, AGAMREE is reaching a growing number of patients worldwide, positioning us well to build on this momentum through the remainder of 2026 and beyond." Operational Highlights (Including post period events) Four of five major EU markets now commercially launched: Pricing and reimbursement agreements were secured in Spain and Italy during the first half of 2026, adding to continued strong commercial momentum in Germany and the UK. Strategic APAC licensing agreement signed with Nxera: Exclusive licensing agreement for Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand valued at up to USD 215 million plus royalties, including USD 30 million in cash and a USD 10 million equity investment in Santhera. Continued progress across mid-sized direct European markets: Swissmedic approved AGAMREE in Switzerland in January 2026, while pricing and reimbursement was agreed in Luxembourg in August, marking the first Benelux market to secure reimbursement. Distributor markets continue to expand: Santhera expanded its agreement with Biomedica to include Georgia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan, while Genesis secured marketing authorization for AGAMREE in Serbia in September, further expanding patient access across its territories. Long-term data further reinforce AGAMREE's differentiated profile: Data from up to eight years of AGAMREE treatment, including baseline results from the ongoing Phase 4 GUARDIAN study, were presented at MDA in March 2026, demonstrating comparable long-term effectiveness to standard-of-care corticosteroids alongside clinically meaningful safety advantages. Additional data and label expansion support continued growth and positioning: CHMP adopted a positive opinion recommending extension of AGAMREE's EU authorization to patients from two years of age, while emerging real-world experience from a case series in adult, non-ambulatory DMD patients presented at ICNMD showed stabilization or improvement in upper-limb function in this patient population. Executive and Board Changes : Orlando Oliveira was appointed CEO in July, Marc Clausse joined as Chief Commercial Officer in June, and Dr. Srishti Gupta was elected to Santhera's Board in May. Financial Highlights Total revenue increased 101% to CHF 48.3 million (H1 2025: CHF 24.0 million), driven by strong growth in product sales and income recognized from the Nxera licensing agreement. Product sales increased 48% to CHF 17.2 million (H1 2025: CHF 11.6 million), reflecting continued strong growth across Santhera's launched markets. Royalties and milestones increased to CHF 29.1 million (H1 2025: CHF 6.5 million), primarily driven by the USD 30 million (CHF 24.2 million) cash upfront payment received under the Nxera licensing agreement. Revenue from the supply of products and services to partners decreased, as expected, to CHF 2.1 million (H1 2025: CHF 5.9 million), primarily reflecting Catalyst's transition to direct sourcing. Global AGAMREE sales, including partner sales, exceeded USD 175 million on a four-consecutive-quarter basis in Q2 2026, triggering a USD 20 million (CHF 16.3 million) sales milestone payment obligation, recognized in cost of sales. Operating expenses decreased 8.4% to CHF 25.0 million (H1 2025: CHF 27.3 million), primarily due to lower development costs. Operating loss narrowed significantly to CHF 6.6 million (H1 2025: CHF 35.4 million). Cash and cash equivalents increased to CHF 41.8 million at June 30, 2026, compared with CHF 22.4 million at December 31, 2025. Full-year 2026 guidance maintained , with total revenue expected to be in the range of CHF 80-90 million. Cash and cash equivalents: While cash is expected to remain broadly stable at 30 September levels through the end of the year, the movement of inventory purchases into Q1 2027, combined with a mandatory German price reduction effective from Q1 2027, is expected to result in a decline in cash during H1 2027, before the Company returns to cash generation in the second half of the year. This change in the cash profile, however, will not require the Company to seek any additional funding. About Santhera Santhera Pharmaceuticals (SIX: SANN) is a Swiss specialty pharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of innovative medicines for rare neuromuscular diseases with high unmet medical need. The Company has an exclusive license from ReveraGen for all indications worldwide to AGAMREE (vamorolone), a dissociative corticosteroid with a novel mode of action, which was investigated in a pivotal study in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) as an alternative to standard corticosteroids. AGAMREE for the treatment of DMD is approved in the U.S. by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), in the EU by the European Commission (EC), in the UK by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), in Switzerland by Swissmedic, in China by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA), in Hong Kong by the Department of Health (DoH) and in Canada by Health Canada. Santhera has out-licensed the rights to AGAMREE as follows: to Catalyst Pharmaceuticals for North America; to Sperogenix Therapeutics for China and certain countries in Southeast Asia; and to Nxera Pharma for Japan, South Korea, Australia, and New Zealand. The Company disclaims any obligation to update these forward-looking statements. # # # Business Review Introduction Santhera continued to make strong progress in the first half of 2026, driven by the expanding commercial rollout of AGAMREE and increasing patient access across both direct and partner markets. Commercial momentum remained strong in Germany and the UK, while pricing and reimbursement agreements in Spain and Italy expanded availability to four of the five major European markets. Beyond Santhera's direct territories, the Nxera licensing agreement significantly extended AGAMREE's commercial reach in APAC, while partners continued to advance access across the US, China and distributor markets. This commercial progress was complemented by new long-term and real-world data further supporting AGAMREE's differentiated profile and its potential across a broader DMD patient population. Advancing the rollout of AGAMREE in Santhera's Major EU Direct markets Commercial uptake of AGAMREE continued to build across Santhera's established European markets during the first half of 2026. In Germany, Santhera's largest market, demand remained strong, with volumes in H1 2026 increasing by more than 50% compared with H1 2025. While the price per bottle decreased to EUR 3,001 in January 2026 from EUR 3,612, reflecting a one-time, pre-agreed price adjustment at the time of initial pricing and reimbursement in early 2025, strong volume growth has more than offset this impact. In the UK, following launch in Q2 2025, uptake continued to progress, supported by increasing systematic adoption across specialist DMD centres and benefitting from updated treatment guidelines and improved access initiatives, including home delivery programs. The publication of the long-term data in March 2026, combined with the access initiatives described above, contributed to orders increasing by more than 40% in Q2 2026 compared with the previous quarter. Significant progress was also made in two of Santhera's largest remaining direct European markets, Spain and Italy, with pricing and reimbursement agreed in both countries during the first half of the year. In Spain, AGAMREE has been available through a named-patient program since mid-2024. In February 2026, AGAMREE was proposed for inclusion in Spain's National Health System, and the launch commenced in Q2. As part of the agreement with the Spanish National Health System and to accelerate patient access to therapy, Santhera provided product free of charge during Q2, with the full commercial sales commencing in July. In Italy, following submission of the long-term data, pricing and reimbursement was agreed in late Q2, with first commercial sales also in July. With AGAMREE now commercially available in four of the five major EU markets, attention is increasingly focused on France. As previously indicated, the French reimbursement process is expected to take longer and will require a full resubmission, this will however benefit from the new positive data that has become available. A commercial launch is therefore not currently expected before 2028, although Santhera is exploring potential routes to accelerate access for French patients. Continued progress in other mid-sized direct EU markets Santhera made further progress on regulatory and reimbursement milestones across its direct European markets during the period. In January 2026, Swissmedic approved AGAMREE for the treatment of DMD in patients aged 4 and older, and post period in August 2026, pricing and reimbursement was agreed in Luxembourg, marking the first Benelux approval. Santhera continues to engage with pricing and reimbursement authorities across the other Benelux countries, the Nordics, Portugal, Switzerland and Ireland. Santhera remains focused on achieving pricing that appropriately reflects AGAMREE's value and is consistent with established major European markets. The Company is also evaluating alternative access pathways where available. Distributor Market - Strong momentum across multiple markets Since July 2024, Santhera has worked closely with Genesis Pharma to advance the phased rollout of AGAMREE across Central and Eastern European markets where Santhera does not sell directly. In September, they secured Marketing Authorization in Serbia, representing a key milestone in the continued expansion of AGAMREE access beyond the EU. Through Genesis Pharma AGAMREE is to date available through various market access pathways in Greece, Cyprus, Malta, the Czech Republic, Poland, Romania, Hungary, Bulgaria, Slovenia, Croatia, Lithuania, and Estonia, with the team looking to expand this further. Commercial momentum across Santhera's distributor markets continued to strengthen during the period, with Genesis and Megapharm delivering strong sales growth alongside increasing contributions from other distribution partners. In July 2026, Santhera further expanded its distribution agreement with Biomedica to include Georgia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan, extending potential access to AGAMREE to an estimated 2,000 additional DMD patients across Central Asia and the Caucasus. Strategic APAC partnership with Nxera In January 2026, Santhera entered into an exclusive licensing agreement with Nxera Pharma for the development, manufacturing and commercialization of AGAMREE in Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand. The agreement is valued at up to USD 215 million plus royalties and included a USD 40 million upfront payment, comprising USD 30 million in cash and a USD 10 million equity investment in Santhera at a 20% premium to the 30-day VWAP prior to the day of announcement. Santhera is also eligible to receive double-digit tiered royalties on net sales in the licensed territories. The partnership significantly expands AGAMREE's commercial reach across the APAC region. In June 2026, AGAMREE was granted ODD and GIFT designations by South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, supporting an accelerated regulatory pathway in the country. Separately, Nxera has indicated it plans to file for regulatory approval for AGAMREE in Japan in the second half of 2027 and to extend AGAMREE into three additional rare disease indications, including Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy, pediatric nephrotic syndrome and juvenile dermatomyositis. Continued strong momentum with US partner Catalyst, now part of Angelini Pharma AGAMREE continued to deliver strong commercial growth in the US during the first half of 2026. Santhera's US partner Catalyst Pharmaceuticals reported AGAMREE net product revenue of USD 36.7 million in Q1 2026, compared with USD 22.0 million in Q1 2025. Prior to its acquisition by Angelini Pharma, Catalyst had guided to FY 2026 AGAMREE net product revenue of USD 140-150 million and reported that 90% of DMD Centers of Excellence had started using AGAMREE for their patients. In May 2026, Angelini Pharma S.p.A. announced an agreement to acquire Catalyst for approximately USD 4.1 billion, with the transaction completing on July 16, 2026. The acquisition established Angelini Pharma's presence in rare diseases and created a commercial presence in the US. In June 2026, Catalyst also reported results from a Phase 1 clinical study suggesting that AGAMREE delivers glucocorticoid and anti-inflammatory activity while avoiding significant immunosuppressive effects at approved dosing, supporting its potential evaluation across a broader range of chronic inflammatory rare diseases. Since mid-2025, Catalyst has held the license to manufacture AGAMREE for North America and has established its own drug product manufacturing capabilities to serve the territory.
